entries.title: II Samuel 12:1
segments: Nathan; a prophet of the Lord.
Men may try ever so much to hide their iniquity, but all who commit it may be sure that in due time their sin will find them out.

entries.title: II Samuel 12:2
segments: Much knowledge of men and much skill are requisite in order most effectually to administer reproof, especially to rulers and men of high rank; and few methods are more suited to this, than wisely selected and graphic illustrations.

entries.title: II Samuel 12:5
segments: Those most indulgent to their own sins, are often most severe against the supposed sins of others.

entries.title: II Samuel 12:6
segments: Fourfold;

Pity for those in distress is a duty so obvious, lovely, and universal, that those who have been most hardened and cruel themselves, when they see in others only a shadow of their own baseness, are ready indignantly to condemn it.

entries.title: II Samuel 12:7
segments: To rulers, as well as all other classes of people, the ministers of God, when called to it, should make a plain, personal, and faithful application of his truth.  Neither fear nor favor should hinder them from pointing out the wickedness of the most exalted sinner, and declaring, Thou art the man.

entries.title: II Samuel 12:9
segments:
Thou hast killed; a man is said to do, and is held responsible for doing, what he causes to be done. 
 
Great mercies bestowed on any one exceedingly aggravate the guilt of his transgressions, and render him deserving of an aggravated punishment.

entries.title: II Samuel 12:10
segments: The sword shall never depart; there would be war and various distresses in his family to the end of his life.
Thou hast despised me; by regarding his own sinful gratification more than the will of God.

entries.title: II Samuel 12:11
segments: I will take thy wives;
God often causes men to read their sins in their punishment, and what they did in secret is punished before the world.

entries.title: II Samuel 12:12
segments: I will do this thing; it would take place in the course of God's providence, through the wickedness of Absalom, in violation of God's law, and to the great distress of David.

entries.title: II Samuel 12:13
segments: Put away thy sin; so forgiven it, in view of his penitence, as expressed in
, that he should not die according to the law,

. 
 
One of the first things in doing good to sinners, is to make them sensible of their sins, and lead them to condemn themselves, and feel that God would be just should he punish them as they deserve.

entries.title: II Samuel 12:14
segments: Though the truly penitent, however great their transgressions, will, for Christ's sake and through faith in him, be forgiven, yet many distressing effects of their sins they may experience to the end of life.

entries.title: II Samuel 12:16
segments: Lay all night upon the earth; in token of his sorrow for sin, his deep humiliatin, and his earnest desire that the child, if consistent with the will of God, might live.

entries.title: II Samuel 12:20
segments:
Washed and anointed--changed his apparel, and--worshipped; in token of his hearty submission to the manifested will of God. 
 
The true penitent, however he may desire and pray that his distresses may be removed or lessened, will heartily submit to those that God lays upon him; feeling that God doeth all things well, and saying, Not as I will, but as thou wilt.  Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him.

entries.title: II Samuel 12:24
segments: Solomon; meaning, peaceable.

entries.title: II Samuel 12:25
segments: Jedidiah; meaning, beloved of the Lord.

entries.title: II Samuel 12:26
segments: Fought against Rabbah; Joab was besieging Rabah when David committed the sin in respect to Uriah.  The sacred writer, having mentioned this great crime, proceeds with the account of its consequences as far as the birth of Solomon, before he returns to the history of the siege of Rabbah.  The capture of that city and the punishment of its people occurred in the interval, certainly before the birth of Solomon, and perhaps before the repentance of David.

entries.title: II Samuel 12:27
segments: The city of waters; that part of the city which supplied the other parts with water; of course the whole must soon surrender.

entries.title: II Samuel 12:31
segments: Under saws; some have supposed the meaning of these words to be, that he put the Ammonites to hard labor with the instruments mentioned. But it is said,

, "he cut them with saws, and with harrows of iron, and with axes."  We must then understand that he put them to torture, or more probably to death, with these instruments; a severity which the sacred writer simply records without in any way expressing approbation of it, and which may have been exercised before his repentance in respect to the matter of Uriah. 
 
  Brickkiln; apparently in a burning state.
